language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi, I'm Chip.
Hi, my name is Abeni.
I live around pyramids and other fun shapes that have been around for thousands of years.
This basket is in the shape of a circle. The distance around the circle is the circumference.
The middle of the circle is the centre. The radius is the distance from the centre to the edge.
The diameter is the distance between two sides of the circle using a straight line that passes through the centre.
Some baskets are half of a circle or a semicircle. A quadrant is a fourth of a circle or half of a semicircle.
The front of this pyramid is a triangle. A triangle has 3 angles that equal 180°.
An equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides and 3 equal angles.
If a triangle has only 2 equal sides and 2 equal angles, it is a isosceles triangle.
If a triangle has one right angle or an angle of 90°, it is a right angle.
From this view, the side looks like a scalene triangle; a scalene triangle has no equal sides and no equal angles.
Wow, they sure knew their triangles when they built the pyramids!
Come on, let’s go have some more fun with circles and triangles.
